title: Just a bit under the kotatsu
setting: A winter morning in Kenta and Sora's flat. Sora's alarm has been going off in his room, and Kenta finds him asleep under the kotatsu.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: sora, okite! sora no heya de, mezamashi zutto natteru yo!
lines.ja: ソラ、起きて！ソラの部屋で、目覚ましずっと鳴ってるよ！
lines.kana: そら、おきて！そらのへやで、めざましずっとなってるよ！
lines.english: Sora, wake up! Your alarm's been going off in your room forever!

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: nande kotatsu de neteru no? futon ni hairanakatta no?
lines.ja: なんでこたつで寝てるの？布団に入らなかったの？
lines.kana: なんでこたつでねてるの？ふとんにはいらなかったの？
lines.english: Why are you sleeping in the kotatsu? Didn't you go to bed?

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: un. ofuro haitte, futon ni hairu mae ni, chotto dake kotatsu ni haitta n da yo.
lines.ja: うん。お風呂入って、布団に入る前に、ちょっとだけこたつに入ったんだよ。
lines.kana: うん。おふろはいって、ふとんにはいるまえに、ちょっとだけこたつにはいったんだよ。
lines.english: Nope. After my bath, I got under the kotatsu for just a bit before going to bed.

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: sou. yoji ni ikkai me ga sameta n da kedo, kimochi yokute okirenakatta.
lines.ja: そう。四時に一回目が覚めたんだけど、気持ちよくて起きれなかった。
lines.kana: そう。よじにいっかいめがさめたんだけど、きもちよくておきれなかった。
lines.english: Yep. I woke up once at four, but it felt so nice I couldn't get up.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.english: You'll catch a cold doing that.

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: kaze wa hiitenai kedo, iya na yume mita. shigoto ni okureru yume.
lines.ja: 風邪はひいてないけど、嫌な夢見た。仕事に遅れる夢。
lines.kana: かぜはひいてないけど、いやなゆめみた。しごとにおくれるゆめ。
lines.english: I haven't caught a cold, but I had a horrible dream. I was late for work.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: aa, kotatsu de neru to, iya na yume miru tte iu yo ne.
lines.ja: ああ、こたつで寝ると、嫌な夢見るって言うよね。
lines.kana: ああ、こたつでねると、いやなゆめみるっていうよね。
lines.english: Oh yeah, they say you get bad dreams if you sleep in the kotatsu.

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: a! shigoto, hachiji kara da! ima nanji?
lines.ja: あ！仕事、八時からだ！今何時？
lines.kana: あ！しごと、はちじからだ！いまなんじ？
lines.english: Oh! Work starts at eight! What time is it?

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: yabai! mezamashi, shichiji ni kaketa noni!
lines.ja: やばい！目覚まし、七時にかけたのに！
lines.kana: やばい！めざまし、しちじにかけたのに！
lines.english: Oh no! I set my alarm for seven!

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: dakara, zutto natteru tte. sono mezamashi de, boku wa me ga sameta n da kedo ne.
lines.ja: だから、ずっと鳴ってるって。その目覚ましで、僕は目が覚めたんだけどね。
lines.kana: だから、ずっとなってるって。そのめざましで、ぼくはめがさめたんだけどね。
lines.english: I told you, it's been going off this whole time. That alarm's what woke me up, you know.

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: gomen! a, shigoto, kyou ja nakute ashita da.
lines.ja: ごめん！あ、仕事、今日じゃなくて明日だ。
lines.kana: ごめん！あ、しごと、きょうじゃなくてあしただ。
lines.english: Sorry! Oh. Work isn't today. It's tomorrow.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: e? jaa, nande mezamashi kaketa no?
lines.ja: え？じゃあ、なんで目覚ましかけたの？
lines.kana: え？じゃあ、なんでめざましかけたの？
lines.english: What? Then why did you set an alarm?

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: kyou da to omotteta. ne, kenta mo kotatsu hairu?
lines.ja: 今日だと思ってた。ね、ケンタもこたつ入る？
lines.kana: きょうだとおもってた。ね、けんたもこたつはいる？
lines.english: I thought it was today. Hey, want to get under the kotatsu too?

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: iya, boku wa futon ni haitte, mou ikkai neru. oyasumi.
lines.ja: いや、僕は布団に入って、もう一回寝る。おやすみ。
lines.kana: いや、ぼくはふとんにはいって、もういっかいねる。おやすみ。
lines.english: Nah, I'm getting back into bed and going back to sleep. Night.

lines.speaker: sora
lines.ja: おやすみ。いい夢見てね。
lines.kana: おやすみ。いいゆめみてね。

choices.english: Sora's alarm never went off, so Kenta woke him just in time for work.
Sora fell asleep under the kotatsu and panicked about work, but his shift is actually tomorrow.
Sora slept through his alarm under the kotatsu and ended up late for his shift.

questions.explanation: Line 4: Sora got under the kotatsu 'just for a bit' before bed (chotto dake kotatsu ni haitta), and line 6: he woke at four but couldn't get up. After his bad dream about being late (line 8), he remembers work starts at eight (line 10) and panics, because it's half past seven (lines 11-12). In line 14 he realises work is tomorrow, not today (kyou ja nakute ashita da), and in line 17 Kenta goes back to bed. A is wrong: the alarm did go off; it has been ringing in Sora's room the whole time (lines 1 and 13), and it woke Kenta up. C is wrong: being late for work only happened in Sora's dream (line 8); his shift is tomorrow (line 14).

questions.english: Sora tells Kenta about the dream he had under the kotatsu. What did he say?
questions.ja: ソラさんは、夢について何と言いましたか？
questions.kana: そらさんは、ゆめについてなんといいましたか？
questions.romaji: sora-san wa, yume ni tsuite nan to iimashita ka?

choices.english: 'There was a bad dream' (aru, word for word)
'I held a bad dream' (motsu, word for word)

questions.explanation: Line 8: iya na yume mita. A dream you have in your sleep is 'seen': yume o miru, here with o dropped and in the past, mita. Kenta uses it again in line 9 (iya na yume miru tte iu yo ne), and Sora signs off with it in line 18 (ii yume mite ne, sweet dreams). A is wrong: yume ga aru (past yume ga atta) is having a dream in the sense of an ambition, like 'I have a dream', not something you see asleep. B is wrong: yume o motsu is also about ambitions (holding a dream for the future); English 'have' doesn't turn into motsu for dreams in your sleep.

questions.english: Sora says, "yoji ni ikkai me ga sameta n da kedo, kimochi yokute okirenakatta." What happened at four o'clock?
questions.ja: 四時に、ソラさんはどうしましたか？
questions.kana: よじに、そらさんはどうしましたか？
questions.romaji: yoji ni, sora-san wa dou shimashita ka?

choices.english: He woke up for a moment, but stayed right where he was under the kotatsu.
He got up, had a bath, and went back under the kotatsu.
His alarm went off, but he slept right through it.

questions.explanation: Line 6: me ga sameta is only the waking, his eyes opening; getting out of bed is okiru, and Sora says okirenakatta (I couldn't get up) because the kotatsu felt so nice (kimochi yokute). English 'woke up' covers both, but Japanese splits them: me ga sameta kedo, okirenakatta. B is wrong: the bath came before he got under the kotatsu (line 4: ofuro haitte), and he never got up. C is wrong: his alarm was set for seven (line 12), not four; at four he woke on his own. Kenta's line 13 shows waking because of an alarm: sono mezamashi de, boku wa me ga sameta.

questions.english: Late at night you're dozing off under the kotatsu. Kenta says, "kotatsu de neru to, kaze hiku yo." (Sleep in the kotatsu and you'll catch a cold.) Tell him you'll get into bed now.
questions.ja: こたつで寝ると、風邪ひくよ。
questions.kana: こたつでねると、かぜひくよ。
questions.romaji: kotatsu de neru to, kaze hiku yo.
questions.answer: Say you'll get into bed with futon ni hairu: wakatta, mou futon ni hairu yo.

modelAnswers.romaji: wakatta. mou futon ni hairu yo.
modelAnswers.ja: 分かった。もう布団に入るよ。
modelAnswers.english: Okay. I'm getting into bed now.

modelAnswers.romaji: sou da ne. sorosoro futon ni hairu yo.
modelAnswers.ja: そうだね。そろそろ布団に入るよ。
modelAnswers.english: You're right. Time I got into bed.

questions.explanation: Getting into bed is going in: futon ni hairu, with the same hairu as ofuro ni hairu and kotatsu ni hairu. Sora strings all three together in line 4 (ofuro haitte, futon ni hairu mae ni, chotto dake kotatsu ni haitta), and Kenta says it in line 17 (futon ni haitte, mou ikkai neru). It means getting under the covers, not yet being asleep; the sleeping itself is neru. In casual speech ni can drop (futon hairu).

questions.english: Kenta checks on you the night before an early shift: "ashita, shigoto hachiji kara da yo ne? okireru?" (Work's at eight tomorrow, right? Will you manage to get up?) Tell him you'll set an alarm, or that you already have.
questions.ja: 明日、仕事八時からだよね？起きれる？
questions.kana: あした、しごとはちじからだよね？おきれる？
questions.romaji: ashita, shigoto hachiji kara da yo ne? okireru?
questions.answer: Use mezamashi with kakeru: un, mezamashi kaketoku yo.

modelAnswers.ja: うん、目覚ましかけとくよ。

modelAnswers.romaji: daijoubu. rokuji ni mezamashi kaketa kara.
modelAnswers.ja: 大丈夫。六時に目覚ましかけたから。
modelAnswers.english: I'll be fine. I've set my alarm for six.

questions.explanation: Alarms are set with kakeru: mezamashi o kakeru, often said the night before as mezamashi kaketoku (-toku = do it in advance). Sora uses it in line 12 (mezamashi, shichiji ni kaketa noni) and Kenta in line 15 (nande mezamashi kaketa no?). English 'set' gives no hint of kakeru; mezamashi o oku would only mean putting the clock down somewhere. For a phone alarm, araamu o setto suru is also fine.

questions.english: You're at home with the kotatsu on. Sora comes in from outside and says, "aa, samukatta! soto, metcha samui yo." (Brr, that was cold! It's freezing out there.) Tell him to get under the kotatsu, or suggest you both do.
questions.ja: ああ、寒かった！外、めっちゃ寒いよ。
questions.kana: ああ、さむかった！そと、めっちゃさむいよ。
questions.romaji: aa, samukatta! soto, metcha samui yo.
questions.answer: Invite him in with kotatsu ni hairu: kotatsu haitte! (get in) or kotatsu ni hairou yo (let's get in).

modelAnswers.ja: こたつ入って！気持ちいいよ。
modelAnswers.english: Get under the kotatsu! It's lovely.

modelAnswers.romaji: sou na n da. jaa, kotatsu ni hairou yo.
modelAnswers.ja: そうなんだ。じゃあ、こたつに入ろうよ。
modelAnswers.english: Oh yeah? Then let's get under the kotatsu.

questions.explanation: You go into a kotatsu just like a bath or a bed: kotatsu ni hairu. Sora uses it in line 4 (chotto dake kotatsu ni haitta) and line 16 (kenta mo kotatsu hairu?), dropping ni the second time, as casual speech does. English 'under' tempts kotatsu no shita, but the verb is simply hairu. Sleeping in it is a different phrase, kotatsu de neru (lines 3 and 9).

newWords.english: ring, go off (an alarm, a phone)
